legalName: Erasure of an Adult Misdemeanor Conviction for Conduct Before Age 18, C.G.S. § 54-142a(f)
publicName: Erase a misdemeanor from something that happened before you turned 18
mechanism: This is an adult record: an adult conviction for conduct committed before the person turned 18. It is not juvenile delinquency relief. Two branches turn on when the offense occurred, and only one of them requires a participant petition.

rationale: The registry declares outputStrategyDeclared 'composed' with compositionMode 'alternative' and two branches, of which only the § 54-142a(f)(1) automatic branch is available:true.
The automatic branch requires no filing, so its required output is a participant instruction.

The § 54-142a(f)(2) petition branch is blocked: no official form was located, JD-CR-202 on its face is a Clean Slate form rather than an (f)(2) form, no custom pleading is approved, and the historical offense-date and classification rule is unresolved. It is a pleading_document unit with a blocked implementation, and nothing is drafted.

authoritySpine.description: The automatic branch. Misdemeanors committed while under 18 where the offense occurred on or after 1 January 2000 and before 1 July 2012 are erased, or deemed erased by operation of law for scanned and non-electronic records.

The petition branch. Where the offense occurred before 1 January 2000, the person may file a petition with the Superior Court at the location where the conviction was effected and the court shall direct erasure.

The same-information limitation. Notwithstanding the multi-count rule at subsection (i), the subsection does not apply where there has been a conviction for any charge for which erasure would not apply arising from the same information as the erased conviction.
Official source recorded on the track, retrieved 2026-07-30.

counselFlags.statement: The § 54-142a(f)(2) petition branch has no identified form and no approved custom pleading. No official form was located for it, and the historical offense-date and classification rule is unresolved.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether the Judicial Branch publishes a form for a § 54-142a(f)(2) petition, or what custom pleading is accepted, and the historical offense-date and classification rule.

counselFlags.statement: JD-CR-202 on its face is a Clean Slate form, not an (f)(2) form. Whether the Judicial Branch publishes a form for a § 54-142a(f)(2) petition, and whether JD-CR-202 is used for it in practice, is an open build blocker. The compiled CT profile points the other way — it treats JD-CR-202 as the vehicle for pre-2000 conviction petitions generally, and the Nationwide inventory holds a copy (CR202.pdf). Do not resolve that conflict by assuming the profile is right.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Whether JD-CR-202 is used in practice for a § 54-142a(f)(2) petition, or whether a different form or pleading is required.

counselFlags.statement: This is an adult record: an adult conviction for conduct committed before the person turned 18. It is not juvenile delinquency relief, and must never be described or routed as such.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That screening copy and routing never treat this track as juvenile relief.

counselFlags.statement: Notwithstanding the multi-count rule at subsection (i), the subsection does not apply where there has been a conviction for any charge for which erasure would not apply arising from the same information as the erased conviction. § 54-142a(f)(3). This route states the rule and draws no conclusion about any participant's information.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That screening asks about other charges on the same information and never infers the answer.

counselFlags.statement: The automatic branch does not reach a motor vehicle offense, a violation under title 14, or a violation of § 51-164r. The participant copies the statute sections from their own record; LegalEase does not classify the offense.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the carve-outs are presented for the participant to apply, not applied to them from an inferred offense classification.

counselFlags.statement: The offense date selects the branch: on or after 1 January 2000 and before 1 July 2012 is the automatic branch; before 1 January 2000 is the petition branch. LegalEase does not choose the branch for the participant and performs no date arithmetic on their behalf.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That screening presents both windows and takes the offense date as a participant answer confirmed against their own case look-up.

counselFlags.statement: The automatic branch is recorded as covering offences on or after 1 January 2000 and before 1 July 2012, and the petition branch as covering offences before 1 January 2000. No source read for this track states what happens to an offence committed on or after 1 July 2012. This route asserts nothing about that window.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: What relief, if any, § 54-142a(f) provides for conduct committed while under 18 on or after 1 July 2012, and which track owns it.

counselFlags.statement: The source review states no service requirement, no notice requirement and no notarization requirement for the (f)(2) petition. None is asserted.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: Service, notice and notarization requirements for the (f)(2) petition, once the vehicle is settled.

counselFlags.statement: No fee. § 54-142a(k). This fee statement is squarely sourced for § 54-142a filings and is stated to the participant. It must not be carried across to § 54-142d, where the fee question is open.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That the § 54-142a(k) fee bar is quoted only for § 54-142a filings.

counselFlags.statement: Automatic erasure stalled for years on data and IT problems and only resumed at scale in late 2025. Never assume a record was auto-erased — verify. A record on the automatic branch that was not erased belongs on the missed-erasure route.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That screening hands a participant whose record was not erased to the missed-erasure route.

counselFlags.statement: Connecticut says erasure. Not expungement, not sealing.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That participant copy for this track uses 'erasure' only.

counselFlags.mustConfirm: That screening stops on an immigration matter on both branches.

omissionProof.statement: units[] enumerates every legal unit the pinned registry entry and the compiled CT profile record for this track. The registry records two alternative branches in units[] — the § 54-142a(f)(1) automatic branch and the § 54-142a(f)(2) petition branch — and one packetSet component (process_guidance). Its one participantFilingRequirement is the Judicial Branch case look-up printout, which the participant obtains and which this route does not produce. The § 54-142a(f)(3) same-information limitation is a rule that constrains both branches, not a separate document. Nothing in either source describes any further document, form, letter or cover sheet for this track.

profilePassageReferenced.passage: Most Connecticut erasure happens automatically with no form. Forms arise for pre-2000 petitions, missed automatic erasures, and pardons. ... JD-CR-202 — Petition for Clean Slate Erasure: convictions entered BEFORE 1/1/2000, filed with the court where sentenced; also the basis for requesting review of a missed automatic erasure.
profilePassageReferenced.reading: The profile records exactly two artefacts on the under-18 path: nothing at all on the automatic side, and a single petition on the pre-2000 side. That matches the two units here. The profile names JD-CR-202 as that petition; the registry says JD-CR-202 is a Clean Slate form and not an (f)(2) form, which is why unit 2 is blocked rather than pointed at CR202.pdf. Either way the profile adds no third unit.
